Hi Emily — thanks for the details and the list. We want to get to a practical solution. Our proposed approach:

1) OSS third‑party claims: Redwood will accept a limited carveout for OSS-origin claims where (a) the component is listed in an agreed "OSS schedule" (OSS_thirdparty_list.csv) and (b) the claim arises solely from the licensed component (not from Customer’s combination or use). When Redwood accepts responsibility, Redwood may exercise subrogation rights against the upstream licensor. We propose an aggregate cap for OSS carveout-related indemnity at USD 500,000 per year for this Order Form.

2) AI-generated output: Redwood will indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the underlying Redwood-provided model weights or model training artifacts infringe a third party’s IP, provided Customer promptly notifies Redwood, cooperates in defense, and allows Redwood to control defense and settlement. We are not offering open-ended indemnity for downstream uses or content created by Customer prompts. Any payments for damages will follow a 30‑day verification/cure process and Redwood will reimburse reasonably documented amounts within 30 days of final determination.

3) Evidence & timing: We agree to specific evidence requirements (e.g., written claim, evidence tying claim to an enumerated OSS component or model artifact) before paying. We can accept a 45-day reimbursement window only if the claim is independently adjudicated or a binding settlement is reached; otherwise, 30 days is our standard operational timeline.

If we can align on the OSS schedule scope and confirm subrogation + the cap, we should be able to finalize the Order Form without escalation. Happy to take a call tomorrow.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Legal — Contracts
Redwood Inference

Appreciate the thoughtful draft. Blueleaf is prepared to accept the approach with two adjustments:

We accept Redwood's limitation on downstream output claims (i.e., not indemnifying customer prompt design/usage) so long as Redwood retains responsibility for model-origin infringement as described.
